review.title: The desktop forwarder spec shares one ledger across parallel workers
review.acceptance: The desktop forwarder spec gives the same answer however many workers Playwright runs it with. It does not today: the stub backend keeps ONE request ledger for the whole process, three tests clear it and then assert it holds exactly their own request, and playwright.config.ts sets fullyParallel: true -- which splits tests WITHIN a file across workers. A two-core machine gets one worker and the file passes; a CI runner gets several and a neighbour's forwarded request lands between the clear and the read. CI run 37007312900 failed exactly that way on three assertions, and --workers=4 reproduces it locally. REQUIRED: the isolation is structural rather than a matter of how many cores the machine running it happens to have. REQUIRED: toHaveLength(1) survives unchanged -- it is the assertion that a forwarder neither retries nor fans out, which the spec records as 'a duplicated session request against a real backend is a duplicated authorization', and relaxing it to 'at least one' would delete the check in order to make the schedule convenient. REQUIRED: the repair is demonstrated under more workers than the machine has cores, because a pass at one worker is what hid this for as long as it was hidden.
review.notes: FILED IN ROUND 104 from CI run 37007312900 on d6d0324, which is the first run after the branch was published. Not caused by that round: neither PW-0309 nor PW-0503 touches this spec, the stub or the forwarder.

typecheck.evidence: cd e2e && npx tsc --noEmit at 2f69f2d07c05bc077505f5d7326ef998a628ba17: exit 0. The spec gained an import of randomUUID from node:crypto and two helpers; the compiler is what caught that the first attempt had the import missing. apps/web npx tsc --noEmit also exit 0, and npm run repo:validate and npm run ai:validate both pass (114 tasks).

e2e.evidence: Playwright 1.62.1, chromium revision 1234, at 2f69f2d07c05bc077505f5d7326ef998a628ba17. fullyParallel stays ENABLED, retries stay 0, no timeout ceiling was raised, and no assertion was weakened -- toHaveLength(1) is unchanged in all three places. PROOF THE OLD IMPLEMENTATION FAILS UNDER REAL PARALLELISM, measured by stashing this commit's change and re-running: --workers=4 gives 1 failed / 8 passed; --repeat-each=3 --workers=4 gives 5 failed / 22 passed. PROOF THE REPAIR HOLDS, same spec, same machine: --workers=4 0 failed; --workers=8 0 failed; --repeat-each=3 --workers=4 27 passed; --repeat-each=5 --workers=8 45 passed. The repeat cases matter as much as the worker cases, because two copies of the same test running at once is the collision a per-invocation identity has to survive and a per-content-id filter would not. WHOLE api PROJECT: 55 passed / 8 skipped at --workers=4 and again at --workers=8. COLLATERAL, whole projects, three configurations, all exit 0: development chromium+api 93 passed / 14 skipped; production no database 61 passed / 46 skipped; production + real PostgreSQL 16.15 at postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl with 8 tables asserted, 76 passed / 31 skipped. apps/web unit suite unaffected at 84 files / 1494 tests. UNVERIFIED AND NOT CLAIMED: whether GitHub CI is green. That is answered only by GitHub executing this commit, which needs a push this session cannot make. gpt's section 5 says it in terms -- do not call CI healthy until GitHub executes the repaired commit.
